welcome_body: Read your own documents and ask about the passages that matter. Your library stays on this Mac.
connect: Use your Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity login
connect_body: CLI providers start disabled. Enable one here to use its login. Discovery and chat may contact provider services and CLI telemetry endpoints. Chat sends questions, conversation history, document metadata and selected text to your chosen provider. You can read without connecting. Without a selection, the document outline and opening excerpt are sent. Earlier selections can remain in conversation history.
signin: Not ready yet? Install the CLI and sign in in Terminal, then check again.
key_saved: Key saved. The connection has not been tested.
bring: Start with something you care about
bring_body: Add your notes, a paper, or a short sample. Your original file is kept alongside a readable copy. The first conversion asks to download packages from PyPI and possibly Python from GitHub. Choose Offline to read Markdown and text; retry conversion when ready.
sample_added: Your sample is in the Library.
coach: Three small ways to go further
coach_body: No setup to perfect. Start with one question.
tip_select: Select a passage, then ask why it matters or request an example.
tip_pin: Pin what you return to. Use folders to give each topic a home.
tip_usage: Keep an eye on Usage. Set a monthly budget at your own pace.
name: Your name (optional)
preview_passage: Reading becomes understanding when we connect new ideas.
preview_question: How does this help me learn?
preview_answer: Link a new concept to something you already know.
setup_help: AI comes from another service. Reading files is free of AI charges. To ask AI, first set up an account with OpenAI or Anthropic. An API key is a secret code from that account; API use can cost extra, even with a chat subscription. CLI means a separate app that you install and sign in to before refreshing this list. You can skip this and read a sample now.
